comments.author: @Annie-BrieL.Hay-Alexis
comments.text:
Can I just say as a former teacher who didn't even make thru her first year as a teacher. I come from a family of teachers and I loved teaching. I loved being in my classroom, being with my students, creating the lesson plans and the curriculum all of it. Wasn't a fan of grading it I was not a big deal compared to being in the classroom everyday.
As much I love the craft and the field of teaching I can see as many of us do that this particular field is pretty much dead. Everyone is fleeing this field like a sinking ship and rightly so. Teachers were and are gaslit into accepting substance standards working conditions that we would never accept at a minimum wage job like a fast food  restaurant or retail store.
After just 7 months of no help and little direction I ended up in the hospital after having a mental breakdown. And the admin treated me like I had abandoned my students to go play hooky. 
During just my first year i had fights in my classroom, had been called racial and demolizing slurs, I've been doxxed, had students out right refuse to do work, and just plain disrupt my class cuz they thought it was funny.
My story is one of probably thousands of teachers across America who are in the same boat as me confused and angry by the level of education we had to have to obtain to work this job only to be treated like glorified babysitters and not like the professional educational and developmental scientist that we actually are.
And much as I love this profession and have to regularly resist the urge to go running back to it like an abusive boyfriend, I think it time to let it die. Let it all collapse and fall completely apart. 
The majority of parents, students and admin do not appreciate the level of work and effort we as educational scientists pour into this field and rightly so because it's given away to them mostly for free. 
I have a deep seated feeling that once this field dies and no one can be convinced to to work these very essential jobs, when parents have to resort to paying full price for their childs/ children's education then we'll start hearing about the "good ole days" of public school.
